name: phase2_tier1_rate
_comment: Tier-1 (RAPL) bit-error rate against symbol rate.
ws_l3_x8 is the transmitter because Phase 1 found it the most detectable
victim, not the one with the largest delta power: ws_dram_x8 moves more
energy per byte but needs n=13-89 samples per decision against n=1-8 here.
Symbol periods run from 2 ms (one RAPL sample per Manchester chip, the
floor the ~1 ms update rate imposes) to 32 ms. Payload sizes are chosen
to keep each run near 5-20 s while putting the most bits at the fast end,
where the errors are; a run with no errors bounds BER only as well as its
bit count allows, which is why the slow rows still carry 616 bits.
The A/A row transmits with on == off, so a decoder that reports anything
but chance on it is finding structure that was never sent.
